page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a nominal clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, yielding a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic processing benefits from hardware-accelerated AES instructions, though x86-specific instruction sets like AVX are absent due to the arm64 platform.

Network throughput is provisioned with a 12 Gbps baseline interface. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data storage and operating volumes rely entirely on network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes. Acceleration hardware is not present, with zero dedicated GPUs assigned to the configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution efficiency across general computing tasks. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng evaluations hit 1707.39 and 6817.26 respectively. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs within the top 25% at 14.43 GB/sec, while Geekbench multi-core registers 5938.0 points. Memory subsystems deliver 96.29 GB/sec in large-block read transfers. In contrast, PassMark CPU benchmarks skew lower, notably in synthetic encryption tests where throughput reaches 750.19. Workloads requiring complex vector execution or large-scale machine learning inference are constrained, as evidenced by low throughput in language model generation tasks.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the c8gn.xlarge provides balanced compute throughput per core on ARM architecture, paired with solid 12 Gbps networking. The platform functions best for network-intensive compute tasks, static web serving, Redis caching nodes, microservices, continuous integration runners, and batch data processing workloads that do not require local disk IOPS or GPU compute.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture and managed by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated arm64 cores running at 2.8 GHz, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the c8gn.xlarge shows balanced mid-tier compute capabilities, recording 5938.0 points in multi-core Geekbench and 9.4 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, alongside strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.43 GB/sec. Compute-heavy mathematical extensions and machine learning inference show lower comparative performance. The configuration is best matched to network-heavy application serving, containerized services, web hosting, and distributed build pipelines.
og_description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance with 4 Neoverse-V2 cores, 8 GB RAM, and 12 Gbps network baseline. It offers balanced compute for web serving and caching.

8.0 GB system RAM providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation
12 Gbps baseline networking throughput via AWS Nitro system
Zero integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage
